question.worked_solution:
We use the change of base formula:

$$
{log}_{a}⁡X=\frac{{log}_{b}⁡X}{{log}_{b}⁡a}
$$

We want to change from base $a=1000$ to base $b=10.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{1000}⁡x & =\frac{{log}_{10}⁡x}{{log}_{10}⁡(1000)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Rewriting the expression in the denominator using exponents, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{log}_{10}⁡x}{{log}_{10}⁡(1000)} & =\frac{{log}_{10}⁡x}{{log}_{10}⁡({10}^{3})} \\  & =\frac{{log}_{10}⁡x}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $\operatorname{log}⁡x=t,$ we conclude that

$$
{log}_{1000}⁡x=\frac{{log}_{10}⁡x}{3}=\frac{t}{3}.
$$
